mainTopic: Communal salt and wood for the מזבח, and mixtures of קמצים and of קרבן blood
overview: The amud opens by finishing an explanation of why בית דין had to let כהנים use the communal salt: otherwise one might think only ישראלים, who pay into the לשכה, could use it. The גמרא then asks how we know the wood on the מזבח is communal. A ברייתא learns from a פסוק linking the wood and fire to the מזבח. רבי אלעזר בר רבי שמעון says they must be communal like the מזבח, while רבי אלעזר בן שמוע says they must never have been used by a הדיוט. The practical difference is whether the wood must be new. A פסוק about ארונה offering threshing tools as wood is answered by saying those tools were new, and the גמרא explains that מוריגים are toothed threshing boards. A new משנה rules that a קומץ mixed with other fully burned מנחות stays כשרה, but רבי יהודה disqualifies mixtures with different amounts of oil. The גמרא brings a משנה about mixed blood. רבי יוחנן shows that both sides learn from the פסוק about mixing the blood of the פר and שעיר on יום כיפור, and the explanation of רבנן's view continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why the stipulation was needed for salt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its answer: without the stipulation, one might think the Torah let only ישראלים, who pay into the לשכה, use the salt, but not כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that when the Torah allowed people to use the salt, it allowed it only to ישראלים, because they pay into the לשכה. כהנים, who do not pay into the לשכה, were not allowed. So the teaching tells us the court gave them the right too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its answer to why בית דין had to stipulate that כהנים may use the communal salt, even though the Torah already allows salt to be used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The salt is bought with money from the לשכה, the half-שקל fund. A person might reason that only those who pay into that fund get to use what it buys. Since כהנים do not pay, the stipulation was needed to include them.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, meaning the Torah or ה׳
The Temple chamber fund, built from the half-שקל donations
Granted them a right
It teaches us, showing the point of a teaching

phrases.english: when the Merciful One granted it [the salt] to them,
it was to Israelites, who have [a share in] the chamber.
To priests, who do not have [a share in] the chamber,
the Merciful One did not grant it to them;
so it teaches us [that the court granted it to them].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes an answer that began before this section
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains a possible mistaken assumption that the teaching comes to rule out
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only ישראלים, who pay into the לשכה, may use the salt.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because of the stipulation of בית דין, כהנים may use it too.

steps.title: Source that the wood is communal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn that the wood for the מזבח comes from the ציבור, as the תנא simply assumes.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא takes it for granted that the wood comes from the community. Where do we learn this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns from salt to wood and asks for the source that the wood belongs to the ציבור. This sets up the ברייתא in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The stipulation about wood only makes sense if the wood is communal property. The תנא treats that as obvious, so the גמרא wants to see where it comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: Wood, here the firewood burned on the מזבח
Obvious
From communal property
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: And the wood,
which is obvious to the tanna that it is from communal property,
from where do we know this?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעֵצִים, דִּפְשִׁיטָא לֵיהּ לְתַנָּא דְּמִשֶּׁל צִיבּוּר, מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the salt to the second item in the stipulation, the wood
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that the wood for the מזבח comes from the ציבור

steps.title: The wood and fire are communal like the altar
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from a פסוק that links the wood and fire to the מזבח: just as the מזבח is communal, so are the wood and fire. This is the view of רבי אלעזר בר רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think that a person who promises to bring an עולה must bring wood from home, just as he brings his own נסכים. So the פסוק says, 'on the wood that is on the fire which is upon the altar.' Just as the altar belongs to the community, the wood and fire belong to the community too. This is the view of רבי אלעזר בר רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא that learns from a פסוק that the wood and fire must come from the ציבור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the owner brings his own נסכים, you might think he also brings his own wood. The פסוק puts the wood right next to the מזבח, so they share the same rule. The מזבח is communal, so the wood is communal too.

keyTerms.meaning: One might have thought, which opens a mistaken assumption
'It is upon me to bring an עולה,' a vow to bring a burnt offering
Libations, the wine and flour offerings that come with a קרבן
The verse comes to teach
Just as… so too…, a comparison between two things

steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is the source that the תנא's stipulation about wood relied on.

phrases.english: As it is taught: One might have thought that one who says,
'It is upon me to bring a burnt offering,'
must bring wood from his home,
just as he brings libations from his home?
The verse states:
'On the wood that is on the fire
which is upon the altar.'
Just as the altar is from communal property,
so too the wood and fire are from communal property.

phrases.aramaic: דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן.
phrases.english: These are the words of Rabbi Elazar bar Rabbi Shimon.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: יָכוֹל הָאוֹמֵר הֲרֵי עָלַי עוֹלָה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק links the wood to the מזבח, so the wood is communal just like the מזבח.

steps.title: A second reading: never used by an ordinary person
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן שמוע reads the same comparison differently: the wood and fire must never have been used by a הדיוט, just like the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר בן שמוע says: just as no ordinary person ever used the altar, so too the wood and fire must be things no ordinary person has used.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings a second תנא who reads the same link between the wood and the מזבח in a different way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both תנאים agree that the wood is compared to the מזבח. They disagree about what the shared feature is. For one it is communal ownership, and for the other it is never having been used for ordinary purposes.

keyTerms.meaning: An ordinary person, meaning ordinary everyday use
Was used

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar ben Shammua says:

phrases.aramaic: מָה מִזְבֵּחַ – שֶׁלֹּא נִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בּוֹ הֶדְיוֹט,
phrases.english: Just as the altar was not used by an ordinary person,
so too the wood and fire
must be ones that an ordinary person has not used.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second reading of the same comparison to the מזבח
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The wood and fire must never have been used by a הדיוט.

steps.title: What is the practical difference?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the two views differ in practice.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a practical case where the two views would rule differently. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both views agree that a person does not bring the wood from his own home, so they seem to lead to the same result. The גמרא wants a case where they split.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the two readings in steps 3 and 4 differ in practice
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A practical case where the two views give different rulings

steps.title: The difference is whether the wood must be new
steps.stepSummary: The difference between them is whether the wood must be new, meaning never used.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is whether the wood must be new.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two views differ about whether the wood must be brand new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אלעזר בר רבי שמעון, communal wood is fine even if it was used before. For רבי אלעזר בן שמוע, the wood must be new and never used.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them
New items that were never used

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אלעזר בן שמוע, wood for the מזבח must be new. According to רבי אלעזר בר רבי שמעון, it only has to be communal.

phrases.english: The difference between them is [whether the wood must be] new.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They differ over whether the wood must be new.

steps.title: ארונה offered used equipment as wood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that used wood is not allowed. ארונה offered דוד the threshing tools and ox equipment to use as wood for an עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is used wood really not allowed? But the פסוק says that ארונה told דוד: let the king take what he wants and offer it. Here are oxen for the burnt offering, and the threshing tools and ox equipment for the wood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the view that the wood must be new, using a פסוק where farm equipment, which seems to have been used, was offered as wood for a קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Threshing tools and ox equipment are normally things that were already used for farm work. If they were fit to burn on the מזבח, then used wood would be allowed, against רבי אלעזר בן שמוע.

keyTerms.meaning: Old items that were used before
But isn't it written?, which opens a challenge from a פסוק
Threshing tools

phrases.english: And old [used wood] is not [fit]?
But isn't it written: 'And Araunah said to David:
Let my lord the king take and offer up
what seems good in his eyes;
see, the oxen for the burnt offering,
and the threshing tools and the equipment of the oxen for the wood'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the requirement of new wood from step 6
steps.kashyaTarget: The requirement that the wood must be new
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Farm tools are normally used ones, yet the פסוק offers them as wood for an עולה.

steps.title: That equipment was new too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the tools ארונה offered were also new.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, the פסוק is talking about new tools.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying that ארונה's tools were new and had never been used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק does not say the tools had been used. If they were new, the פסוק does not contradict the view that the wood must be new.

keyTerms.meaning: Here too

steps.whatToRemember: The פסוק about ארונה does not prove that used wood is allowed, because the גמרא explains that his tools were new.

phrases.english: Here too, it is speaking of new ones.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Reads the case in the פסוק narrowly, as new tools
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The tools were used, which would show that used wood is allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The tools were new, so there is no contradiction.

steps.title: What does the word מוריגים mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what מוריגים means, the word used for the tools ארונה offered to דוד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes a short side trip to ask what the word מוריגים means. This question sets up the explanation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 7, ארונה offered דוד his מוריגים as wood for the עולה. Nothing in the halacha depends on this question. The גמרא simply wants to understand the word.

keyTerms.meaning: Threshing sledges, the tools ארונה offered to דוד

phrases.english: What are 'morigim'?
phrases.notes: This is the word from the ארונה story in step 7 (שמואל ב 24:22).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side question about a word in the פסוק quoted in the קשיא of step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word מוריגים.

steps.title: עולא explains: a threshing board
steps.stepSummary: עולא says מוריגים means a מטה של טרבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: a מטה של טרבל.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא answers that מוריגים is a 'מטה של טרבל', which is a kind of board.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא uses a phrase from his own place, ארץ ישראל. People in בבל did not know it, so his answer still needs its own explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'turbal bed', a flat board used for threshing

phrases.english: Ulla said:
A turbal bed.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מוריגים are a מטה של טרבל.

steps.title: What is a מטה של טרבל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what עולא's phrase means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is a מטה של טרבל?
steps.whatsHappening: עולא's answer was itself unclear, so the גמרא asks what a מטה של טרבל is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a follow-up question. The explanation of the word is not finished until we know what this object actually is.

phrases.english: What is a turbal bed?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: What object a מטה של טרבל is.

steps.title: רב יהודה: a jagged threshing board
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה explains that it is a toothed board that threshers use.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: a serrated board that the threshers thresh with.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה explains that a מטה של טרבל is a board with sharp teeth that threshers drag over grain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the word is fully explained. ארונה was offering his threshing boards, and they were made of wood, so they could be burned for the עולה.

keyTerms.meaning: A board with jagged, saw-like teeth
Threshers, people who thresh grain

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
A serrated board
that the threshers thresh with.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is a toothed board used for threshing grain.

steps.title: רב יוסף brings a פסוק for the meaning
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף shows from a פסוק in ישעיה that a מורג is a toothed threshing tool.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: What is the verse? 'Behold, I have made you a new threshing sledge, sharp, with teeth; you shall thresh the mountains.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף brings a פסוק as a source for this meaning of the word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes a מורג that is sharp, has teeth, and is used for threshing. That matches רב יהודה's explanation exactly, so the meaning is now backed by a פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the פסוק (the source in the text)?
Threshing sledge
Sharp edges or teeth

steps.whatToRemember: מוריגים are wooden threshing boards with teeth. That is why ארונה could offer them as wood for the מזבח.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: What is the verse?
'Behold, I have made you a threshing sledge,
sharp, new, having teeth;
you shall thresh the mountains.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב יהודה's explanation with a פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: The meaning of מורג as a toothed threshing board.

steps.title: משנה: a mixed-up קומץ is still fit
steps.stepSummary: If a קומץ gets mixed with another קומץ, or with מנחות that are burned completely, the mixture is כשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If its handful became mixed with the handful of another meal offering, or with the meal offering of priests, or with the meal offering of the anointed priest, or with the meal offering of libations, it is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. The קומץ of a regular מנחה got mixed with another קומץ, or with a מנחה that is burned whole, and the ruling is that it is still כשרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everything in this mixture goes onto the מזבח anyway. So mixing them together does not ruin anything, and the whole mixture is burned.

keyTerms.meaning: The handful taken from a מנחה and burned on the מזבח
A מנחה brought by a כהן, which is burned completely
The daily מנחה of the כהן גדול, which is burned completely
The מנחה that comes with a קרבן's wine offering, which is burned completely

phrases.english: MISHNA:
If its handful became mixed with the handful of another meal offering,
or with the meal offering of priests,
or with the meal offering of the anointed priest,
phrases.notes: The 'anointed priest' is the כהן גדול.

phrases.english: or with the meal offering of libations, it is fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה starts, after the side discussion about wood ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A קומץ mixed with another קומץ or with a fully burned מנחה stays כשרה.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: some mixtures are unfit
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says a mixture with מנחת כהן משיח or מנחת נסכים is פסולה, because the different oil levels soak into each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: with the meal offering of the anointed priest or the meal offering of libations, it is unfit, since this one's mixture is thick and that one's mixture is loose, and they absorb from each other.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה disagrees with part of the משנה. He says a mixture with מנחת כהן משיח or מנחת נסכים is פסולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A regular מנחה has less oil, so it is 'thick'. מנחת כהן משיח and מנחת נסכים have much more oil, so they are 'loose'. When they mix, oil moves from one to the other, and each one ends up with the wrong amount of oil.

keyTerms.meaning: The mixing of flour with oil
Thick, meaning a mixture with less oil
Loose or soft, meaning a mixture with more oil
They absorb or soak in

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה does not argue about a קומץ mixed with another קומץ or with מנחת כהנים. He only argues about the two kinds that have extra oil.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: בְּמִנְחַת כֹּהֵן מָשִׁיחַ, בְּמִנְחַת נְסָכִים – פְּסוּלָה,
phrases.english: with the meal offering of the anointed priest or the meal offering of libations, it is unfit,
since this one's mixture is thick,
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the regular קומץ, which has less oil.

phrases.english: and that one's mixture is loose,
and they absorb from each other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with part of the תנא קמא's ruling in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A mixture with a מנחה that has a different oil level is פסולה, because the oil passes between them.

steps.title: A related משנה about mixed blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה in זבחים: blood mixed with water, wine, or animal blood is judged by whether it still looks like blood. רבי יהודה says blood does not cancel out blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: We learned there: Blood that became mixed with water, if it has the appearance of blood, it is fit. If it became mixed with wine, we view the wine as if it were water. If it became mixed with the blood of a domesticated animal or an undomesticated animal, we view that blood as if it were water. רבי יהודה says: Blood does not nullify blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by quoting a different משנה, about קרבן blood that got mixed with other liquids. This is setting up the next move, which will connect it to our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that the mixture is fit if the קרבן blood would still show its look, with the other liquid treated as plain water. רבי יהודה says that ordinary blood cannot cancel קרבן blood. רבי יהודה ruled about mixtures in our משנה too, and that is likely why the גמרא brings this source.

keyTerms.meaning: The look of blood
We imagine it as if it were water
Blood does not cancel out blood

phrases.english: GEMARA: We learned there:
Blood that became mixed with water,

phrases.aramaic: אִם יֵשׁ בּוֹ מַרְאִית דָּם – כָּשֵׁר.
phrases.english: if it has the appearance of blood, it is fit.
If it became mixed with wine,
we view it as if it were water.
phrases.notes: Red wine looks like blood, so we picture it as water to see if the קרבן blood would still show.

phrases.aramaic: נִתְעָרֵב בְּדַם בְּהֵמָה אוֹ בְּדַם חַיָּה –
phrases.english: If it became mixed with the blood of a domesticated animal or of an undomesticated animal,
we view it as if it were water.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
Blood does not nullify blood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא on our משנה opens by bringing a related משנה about mixtures, to set up a discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Mixed קרבן blood is fit if it would still look like blood when the other liquid is pictured as water. רבי יהודה says blood does not cancel blood.

steps.title: Both sides learn from one verse
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says that רבנן and רבי יהודה both base their views on the same פסוק: "And he shall take of the blood of the bull and of the blood of the goat."
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Both of them learned their view from one verse: "And he shall take of the blood of the bull and of the blood of the goat."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן tells us where the מחלוקת about blood mixed with blood comes from. Both sides learn it from the same פסוק about the יום כיפור service.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 16, רבנן and רבי יהודה argued about whether blood can cancel out blood. רבי יוחנן says they are not using different sources. They read the same פסוק, where the כהן גדול takes blood from both the פר and the שעיר together, and they understand it differently.

keyTerms.meaning: One verse
They learned it out from the verse
A bull. Here, the bull the כהן גדול brings on יום כיפור
A goat. Here, the goat brought on יום כיפור

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the disagreement is about how to read one פסוק, not a clash between two different sources.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
And both of them derived it from one verse,
phrases.notes: "Both of them" means רבנן and רבי יהודה from the blood argument we just saw.

phrases.english: "And he shall take of the blood of the bull
and of the blood of the goat."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the shared scriptural source behind the מחלוקת between רבנן and רבי יהודה in step 16
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both רבנן and רבי יהודה build their view on the פסוק about mixing the blood of the פר and the שעיר on יום כיפור.

steps.title: The bull has more blood, and the view of רבנן begins
steps.stepSummary: Everyone knows a פר has more blood than a שעיר. Then רבי יוחנן begins to explain how רבנן read the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a known fact that the blood of a bull is more than the blood of a goat. רבנן hold:
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן continues by pointing out a fact that makes the פסוק puzzling: the bull's blood is much more than the goat's. Then he opens with "רבנן סברי", setting up the explanation of רבנן's view, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the bull's blood is the majority, you would expect the goat's blood to be cancelled in it. Yet the פסוק still calls it "the blood of the goat." Each side will now use this point to support its own view, starting with רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a known fact
More, larger in amount
The Sages, here the תנא קמא who argues with רבי יהודה

steps.confusionAlert: This step does not yet tell us what רבנן learn. "רבנן סברי" is only the opening words, and their reasoning comes right after this.

phrases.english: It is a known matter
that the blood of a bull is more
